title: How to rent a flat in Germany
description: Where to search, what landlords ask for, how the application works and how to improve your chances in a tight market.
html:
Renting in Germany is straightforward once you know the rules, but the rules are not obvious to newcomers. Landlords expect a specific set of documents, viewings are competitive in the big cities, and there are a few local customs that surprise people. Here is how the process works from the first search to the signed contract.

First steps

Decide what you can pay: a common rule is that rent should not exceed a third of your income, and landlords apply the same rule when they check applicants. Learn the two rent figures: Kaltmiete is the base rent, Warmmiete includes heating and service charges, and listings quote either. Have your documents ready before you start viewing.

Types of rental

Unfurnished flats are the norm for long-term rentals and often come without a kitchen; furnished flats and rooms cost more but suit the first year. Sublets (Untermiete) and shared flats are the quickest to get. Temporary furnished rentals of one to twelve months are a growing market aimed at newcomers.

Where to search

The large national listing portals carry most private-market flats; shared-flat platforms carry rooms; the housing associations and cooperatives in each city rent directly, often more cheaply, but with waiting lists. Platforms that specialise in international tenants let you book from abroad, which solves the problem of viewing in person.

The application

A landlord will typically ask for a completed self-disclosure form, a copy of your ID or passport, your last three payslips or proof of income, a credit report from the national credit agency and a letter from your previous landlord confirming that you paid your rent. Students and new arrivals substitute a guarantor's declaration, a scholarship confirmation or a Blocked Account statement for the income proof.

Four things that improve your chances

  • Arrive at viewings with a complete document folder; many people do not.
  • Write a short, polite message with your application explaining who you are and why the flat suits you.
  • Be flexible on move-in dates and neighbourhoods.
  • Reply fast. Flats in Munich and Berlin are gone within days.

Renting a house

Houses are rented the same way but are rarer in cities and usually require a longer commitment. Expect to handle garden maintenance and some repairs yourself, and read the contract for who pays for what.
